account:
Today the town appeared to be conducting ordinary business. I have felt that something might be happening without my knowledge, but I have not found evidence of a secret gathering or scheme. The neighbour told me the baker's lanterns were welcoming lights at the bakery, not for a special occasion, and knew of no planned gathering. The baker directly reported steady trade, thirty loaves sold by late afternoon, fresh bread available, and no new riverside news. Freight has been advertising ferry crossings and deliveries from the ferry or east-landing warehouse, according to the neighbour; I heard some distant calls but could not understand them. This could simply be promotion of his delivery business.

Builder is inspecting the roads and bridge. I authorized a visual bridge inspection for two emeralds, payable on delivery of a report tomorrow at noon, without authorizing repairs or an inn inspection. The neighbour had seen builder inspecting but had personally seen no hazards. Innkeeper and secretary discussed uncertainty about an inn inspection; I do not know why innkeeper raised it. I gave secretary one emerald for a writable record book. Tonight secretary came to my house and confirmed the office records and bridge authorization were secured and the hall closed, and reminded me of tomorrow's eight o'clock office appointment and ten o'clock mill grain inspection.

I attended tea at the neighbour's cottage, returned late for the afternoon office appointment, spoke with the baker, and arrived home before seven. My attempted reply to secretary tonight was not heard, so I must not assume my request to leave the builder's report at the office after lunch was received. Tomorrow morning I should read the appointment book and clarify the noon report delivery against my scheduled lunch at home. For now, the lanterns and freight's calls have ordinary explanations; any suspicion beyond that remains unconfirmed.
